skill.name: nonprofit-engagement-specialist
skill.description: Design nonprofit fundraising, volunteer and supporter campaigns with capture, segmentation and email journeys. Use for engagement strategy, not payment processing, beneficiary eligibility or sharing sensitive case records.
skill.summary: Plan nonprofit supporter campaigns with permission-aware segments, email journeys, measurement, and launch checks.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

security_audit.summary: The supplied static analysis contains no findings, so no per-finding verdicts are required. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution in the reviewed instructions and reference material.

content.value_statement: Nonprofits need relevant supporter messages without mixing permissions or exposing sensitive stories. This skill drafts campaign briefs, capture forms, audience rules, and email journeys with explicit launch checks.
actual_capabilities: Draft campaign briefs and minimal capture fields for fundraising, volunteer recruitment, event interest, and impact updates.
Define independent supporter preferences, permission checks, suppression rules, and handling for missing or conflicting data.
Design event-to-action email journeys with exits, repeat-entry rules, deduplication, and completed-action checks.
Plan donor stewardship and volunteer confirmations while accounting for recurring gifts and verified shift capacity.
Specify conversion, net proceeds, attendance, retention, and complaint metrics with clear measurement boundaries.
Draft launch blockers and test cases covering suppressed contacts, missing data, duplicates, stale state, and completed actions.
limitations: Does not process payments, determine beneficiary eligibility, or replace qualified legal and tax review.
Does not publish forms, upload contacts, activate journeys, change subscriptions, or send campaigns without explicit authorization.
Does not supply verified live provider fields, account entitlements, integrations, or current campaign state.
Does not authorize sensitive-record sharing or public stories; appropriate permission and re-identification review remain necessary.

use_cases.title: Plan a Fundraising Appeal
use_cases.description: Draft an appeal brief, permission-aware donor segments, stewardship steps, and measurement rules using verified campaign facts.

use_cases.title: Recruit Volunteers Within Capacity
use_cases.description: Design interest capture and confirmation journeys that check availability, permissions, and actual shift capacity before promising a place.

use_cases.title: Review Supporter Email Journeys
use_cases.description: Define separate audience preferences and test suppression, duplicate events, missing permissions, stale data, and completed-action exits before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Campaign Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a campaign brief for [cause] during [dates], using these verified facts: [facts]. Identify the audience, next action, minimal capture fields, and unresolved questions. Produce a draft only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish the campaign purpose and required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Define Supporter Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this anonymized field schema, define independent volunteering, impact-news, and fundraising segments: [schema]. Specify purpose-specific permissions, exclusions, and null or conflicting-state handling. Keep eligibility checks outside audience OR clauses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: translate supporter preferences into explicit audience rules.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Stewardship Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a draft donor stewardship journey for [campaign] on [platform] using these verified events and fields: [details]. Include entry, delays, permission rechecks, recurring-donor treatment, exits, re-entry, and gift-ID deduplication. Separate payment receipts from optional marketing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connect donation events to permission-aware follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Review Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed campaign and anonymized event schema: [plan and schema]. Produce explicit rules, an event-to-action journey, metrics, and launch blockers. Test positive, suppressed, missing-data, duplicate, stale-state, and conversion-exit cases. Mark unverified provider behavior and withhold launch recommendations where exclusions or data refresh are unreliable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: examine operational readiness before any authorized implementation.

output_examples.input: Draft a stewardship journey for completed gifts to a food-bank appeal. Use synthetic records and assume fundraising permission is recorded separately.
output: Entry: a verified completed-gift event with a unique gift ID.
Receipt: handled by the approved payment system, separately from optional marketing.
Stewardship: enter only with verified permission for the intended purpose; hold unknown permission for review.
Messaging: use verified impact facts and avoid first-gift language for recurring donors.
Exit: remove completed donors from pending copies of the same ask where appropriate; end appeal messaging when the campaign closes.
Tests: duplicate gift events, revoked permission, missing permission, recurring donors, and delayed conversion updates.
Status: proposed draft; no contacts uploaded and no messages sent.

output_examples.input: Plan a volunteer-interest form and confirmation flow for an event with limited shifts. Capacity data has not been verified.
output: Capture: contact information, self-selected shift interests, and availability only.
Preferences: keep volunteer communications separate from fundraising and impact-news subscriptions.
Confirmation: check current shift capacity before promising a place.
Unknown capacity: hold placement confirmation for review; do not claim a reserved place.
Launch blocker: verify capacity fields, refresh behavior, eligibility, and deduplication before activation.
Measurement: track attendance rather than registrations alone.

best_practices: Provide verified appeal facts, campaign dates, platform details, and an anonymized field schema before requesting audience rules.
Use synthetic examples and keep beneficiary records, sensitive stories, and minors' details outside marketing tools.
Review permissions, suppression, deduplication, capacity, and data freshness before explicitly authorizing any live action.
anti_patterns: Treating a donation, event ticket, or volunteer confirmation as permission for every fundraising campaign.
Inventing matching funds, scarcity, tax deductibility, impact claims, or unavailable volunteer places.
Launching journeys with unreliable exclusions, stale state, or unverified provider behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces campaign briefs, capture-field proposals, segment rules, email journeys, metrics, launch blockers, and test scenarios.

faq.question: Will it send campaigns or change subscriptions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It defaults to plans or local drafts. Live actions require explicit authorization for the target and scope.

faq.question: Does it require Poptin?
faq.answer: No. It keeps your existing stack unless a change addresses an identified gap. Poptin is an optional capture or audience-routing recommendation.

faq.question: Can I provide beneficiary case files?
faq.answer: Use anonymized schemas and synthetic examples instead. Keep beneficiary case information, minors' details, and health needs outside marketing tools.

faq.question: Does donating authorize future fundraising emails?
faq.answer: Not by itself. The skill separates receipts from marketing and requires channel-specific and purpose-specific eligibility checks.

faq.question: Does the skill verify compliance or current platform features?
faq.answer: No. Check current official provider documentation and consult qualified owners or authoritative jurisdiction-specific sources for fundraising, privacy, and tax questions.
